why.rules.level_down: v1 used down = 500 against up = 7 000–17 000 and required an average above 0, so a level never dropped (BUG-TR-02). 3.0–3.2: a result under 40 % of up cost a step, three at an empty bar dropped the level — on a hard level the average player fell back again and again (Guess Who hard: in 100 % of the climbs). 3.2.1 (owner): a level drops only on systematic failure — five results under 40 % of up in a row with no step on this level yet; a weak game never takes a step back (step_loss false). Two good games bring a dropped level back (return_gap 2).
why.rules.brain_power: v1 added trunc(score*15/up) − 5, so a weak result lowered Brain Power below a zero result. Now the played-game part is round(15 × min(score/up, 2)).
why.rules.test: Brain Mark of the profile is the mean of the first three tests (index_tests); after that every new test moves it a third of the way to its result. 3.2–3.4 used the mean of the last three tests: the new test replaced the oldest one, so after 16 % of the tests the number moved against the result of the test, and «+1 to the next rank» stayed after a test above the number in 27 % of such cases. Now a test above the number always raises it, the error of the number is 2.8 points instead of 3.6 and the 90 % band ±5.0 instead of ±6.2. The band: the spread of one test comes from the differences of consecutive tests, pooled with default_sd 7 at the weight prior_weight 4 (it covers the true level of a stable player in 90 % of cases). The rank is taken from the whole number on the screen; it goes up at the threshold and down only more than rank_shield 3 points under it: 27 % of stable players see a demotion in 11 tests instead of 59 %, the rank equals the true one in 84.5 % of tests instead of 80.8 %. The order of games follows a 5×5 Latin square (docs/analytics/test-index.md, test-scale.md).
why.rules.facts: 3.10 (owner: the lists grew to 180, so two open a day). A finished training opens the next fact and the joke with the same number, up to per_day 2 a day: two trainings in a day open two of each, a day without a training opens nothing. The list of data/facts.json holds 180 facts: the 110 of 3.8-3.9 and 70 more written and checked against sources in 3.10 (docs/facts-review.md); data/jokes.json holds 180 jokes (docs/humor.md). Earlier paces: 3.7 opened up to three a day (a list of 222 entries), 3.8-3.9 one a day (110). The code reads per_day, so the pace is one number here.
why.rules.test.shown_level: 3.6 (owner: Arithmetics in the test is a medium task, there are no numbers above 100; keep the task, fix the name). The level a test task is shown as — in the task sheet, the header of the game and the list of the test — and under which its result goes to the records and the achievements. The tasks keep their ids and conditions (1032 and 1112 are «hard» ids of the original), so the marks and the tables do not change. Arithmetics: 12 examples, numbers 12–99 with all four operations (training Medium 10–99, Hard 15–150). Quadronica: the 7 × 10 field with 5 colours — the Medium field of training (Hard is 8 × 11). Guess Who (the Hard layout, 7 rounds), Memorics and Numbers (Medium) already had the right name.
